title: What state and exit code does Docker report?
summary: List stopped containers and inspect the selected container before restarting it.
why: Exit code and state narrow whether the process completed, failed, was killed, or never started correctly.

commands.purpose: Inspect state, exit code, error, command, and restart policy. Output may include environment or configuration values; do not share it without redaction.

choices.label: State or exit code is unclear

title: Was this container intended to be a long-running service?
summary: Exit code 0 means the configured process completed successfully, not that the desired service remained available.
why: Containers stop when their main process exits.

choices.label: It is a one-shot job or expected task

title: What do the container logs show near startup?
summary: Read the failure output before changing restart behavior.
why: Application logs often identify missing configuration, permissions, dependency failure, or command errors.

title: Do inspect details show an engine or startup error?
summary: Review State.Error, Path, Args, mounts, environment names, and restart count without exposing secret values.
why: Some failures occur before application logging starts.

title: Review image command and entrypoint
summary: Compare the image configuration and runtime override with the executable actually present in the image.
why: A wrong command, shell assumption, path, or entrypoint override can make the main process exit immediately.
prerequisites: Review Dockerfile CMD/ENTRYPOINT and runtime overrides.
Test changes in a non-production environment.
rollback: Restore the previous image or runtime command.

choices.label: A reviewed command/image fix was deployed

title: Correct required configuration safely
summary: Review required environment, mounted files, working directory, and application configuration without exposing secret values.

title: Review user, ownership, and mounted-path access
summary: Determine which UID/GID runs the process and whether mounted paths permit the required access.
prerequisites: Inspect image user and host/volume ownership.
rollback: Restore previous ownership or permission settings.

choices.label: A scoped permission fix was applied
The correct ownership model is unclear

title: Is the dependency addressable and ready from the container context?
summary: Confirm names, ports, network attachment, credentials, and readiness assumptions.

choices.label: A dependency or startup-order issue was corrected

title: Review memory usage and limits before restarting
summary: OOM termination requires understanding workload demand and configured limits, not only adding a restart policy.
prerequisites: Confirm OOM evidence and current memory limits.
Review application memory behavior and host capacity.
rollback: Restore prior limits or image if a change worsens stability.

choices.label: A reviewed memory fix was applied

title: Verify process and application health
summary: Confirm more than a running container state.

commands.purpose: Confirm runtime state and recent logs.

verification: The intended process remains running for an appropriate observation period.
The original error is absent from logs.
The application endpoint or job result behaves as expected.

choices.label: The container still exits or is unhealthy

title: Expected one-shot completion
summary: The container completed with exit code 0. Verify the job output rather than forcing it to stay running.
prevention: Document expected lifecycle and success criteria.

title: Recovery verified
summary: Record the actual cause and add health, configuration, or resource checks that would detect recurrence earlier.
prevention: Monitor restart count and termination reasons.

title: Escalate with state, logs, and image context
summary: Share redacted inspect state, exit code, recent logs, image digest, and runtime command with the image or service owner.
